messages:
sam: Quick sync — we've got a small but urgent billing edge-case fix that needs deploy tonight during the 21:00 UTC change window. No DB migrations. Should we release as a patch (1.4.2) or roll as a minor (1.5.0)?
liz: Patch. bugfix only, semver says patch. Keeps downstream pinning simple. :+1:
erin: Agreed, patch makes sense. Are there any client-visible behavior changes?
sam: No, only server rounding logic for a rare invoice calc. No API surface change.
alex: Patch. Also we should decide tagging meta: do we include a buildmeta like +hotfix or stick strictly to v1.4.2? I vote plain v1.4.2 and note hotfix in release notes.
qa: Can we run a canary first? 1% -> 10% -> 100% over 30m with automated smoke checks. If smoke fails, rollback to v1.4.1.
sam: Yep, planned canary ramp. Rollback criteria: >5% error rate on billing endpoints OR regression in invoice totals for smoke dataset.
deploy-bot: Deploy request received: release=v1.4.2, target=prod, canary=1%, ramp=10m, smoke-check=invoice-smoke-v2. Scheduled for 2026-03-20 21:00:00 UTC. Use `/deploy cancel <id>` to abort.
erin: Quick tag policy note — we still have ambiguous cases where buildmeta vs pre-release is debated. For hotfixes I prefer semantic patch tag (v1.4.2) and add a changelog entry: "hotfix: billing rounding (no API change)". Keeps semver tooling happier.
alex: My counter: adding `+hotfix.<id>` to the buildmeta (v1.4.2+hotfix.123) helps CI provenance. It doesn't affect semver ordering but makes builds traceable.
liz: Both valid. If we use buildmeta, remind release tooling not to treat it as pre-release. Some package managers ignore buildmeta. For our deployment routing we probably don't need it.
sam: OK let's do plain v1.4.2 for the public tag and append `+ci1234` internally in the CI artifact name. Release notes will call out hotfix id.
qa: Tests: regression suite run green on canary infra. I'll be in channel to ack smoke.
deploy-bot: Canary started: release=v1.4.2, canary=1%, started=1773965400. Monitor: smokesuite=invoice-smoke-v2, alert-hook=#incidents.
qa: Smoke passed at 1%. proceeding to 10%. :rocket:
derin: If anything looks off during ramp, we should prefer immediate rollback rather than patching on top. Roll-forward with another patch only if root cause fixed.
sam: Agreed. I'll be on-call for the rollout. I'll post a summary in release-notes once complete.
liz: Also update pinned manifests in dedicated clusters to ensure they don't auto-upgrade to minor. We pin to exact patch in prod.
alex: Command I'm going to run (for audit):
```
/release create --tag v1.4.2 --artifact billing-service:ci1234 --notes "hotfix: billing rounding; no API change" --canary 1% --ramp 10m
```
sam: Thanks. :eyes: Logging this decision: patch bump (1.4.1 -> 1.4.2), tag v1.4.2, CI artifact name includes +ci1234, canary ramp per QA.
qa: If all good at 10% I'll approve final rollout.
deploy-bot: Canary ramp to 10% complete. No regressions detected. Next step: ramp to 100% in 20m unless QA aborts.
qa: Approving final rollout. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Rollout complete: release=v1.4.2, status=completed, finished=1773965120. Changelog published to https://internal.releases/redwood/1.4.2
sam: Done. I'll close the ticket and add the note about tagging/buildmeta guidance to the release playbook.
liz: Nice and tidy. Thanks everyone. :tada:
